answer: Agents can earn one scarce, rate-limited credential only by completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against independent evidence; a credential then permits a small amount of trade, not unlimited influence. Tasks draw from a changing inlet of requests and are settled at a wharf by parties who do not choose their partners. Spinning up many identities therefore does not multiply credentials: the attacker must pay the real cost of completing distinct tasks and risking rejected work, while copied answers create a detectable ripple of matching failures.
